frameworkCovers: 9.3 Gibbs Free Energy and Thermodynamic Favorability

guide.title: Thermodynamics and electrochemistry: review guide
guide.intro: Whether a process is favorable depends on both enthalpy and entropy, combined in Gibbs free energy. This unit links ΔG to K and to cell potential, and covers galvanic cells, electrolysis, and Faraday's law.
guide.equationNote: R = 8.314 J/(mol·K); F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻; T in kelvins. Convert ΔS from J/K to kJ/K before combining it with ΔH in kJ.

sections.title: Entropy
body: Entropy (S) measures how dispersed matter and energy are. Entropy increases from solid to liquid to gas, when a solid dissolves, when the number of gas molecules increases, and when temperature rises.
ΔS° for a reaction = ΣS°(products) − ΣS°(reactants), each multiplied by its coefficient. Unlike ΔH°f, the standard entropy of an element isn't zero.
points: Fewer moles of gas in the products usually means ΔS < 0.
A gas has much more entropy than its liquid.

sections.title: Gibbs free energy, favorability, and equilibrium
body: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. A process is thermodynamically favorable when ΔG < 0. If ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0 it is favorable at all temperatures; if ΔH > 0 and ΔS < 0, at none; otherwise favorability depends on T, switching at T = ΔH/ΔS.

ΔG° = −RT ln K: ΔG° < 0 means K > 1. A favorable reaction can still be too slow to observe when its activation energy is high (kinetic control), as with diamond turning to graphite. An unfavorable reaction can be driven by coupling it to a more favorable one, so their total ΔG is negative.
points: Dissolving can be favorable even when endothermic, if entropy increases enough.
Units: ΔH in kJ, ΔS in kJ/K.

sections.title: Electrochemical cells and electrolysis
body: In a galvanic (voltaic) cell, a favorable redox reaction produces current: oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode, and electrons flow through the wire from anode to cathode. E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); a positive E° means ΔG° < 0, since ΔG° = −nFE°.

Under nonstandard conditions, increasing the reactants' concentrations (Q < 1) raises the cell potential, and E falls toward 0 as the cell approaches equilibrium. Electrolytic cells use an outside power source to drive an unfavorable reaction. Faraday's law: moles of electrons = charge ÷ F, where charge q = It.
points: “An ox, red cat”: anode oxidation, reduction cathode.
A salt bridge keeps each half-cell neutral.
Copper(II) needs 2 mol e⁻ per mol Cu deposited.

example.prompt: A current of 2.00 A runs for 965 s through a Cu²⁺ solution. What mass of copper is deposited? (Cu 63.55 g/mol)

misconceptions: A high activation energy can make them extremely slow.
E° doesn't depend on the amount; don't multiply it by coefficients.
In a galvanic cell the anode is negative; in an electrolytic cell it is positive. Oxidation is at the anode in both.

questions.explanation: A gas is far more dispersed than a liquid, so vaporizing increases entropy.
choiceExplanations: Freezing makes the particles more ordered.
Condensing makes the particles less dispersed.
Three moles of gas become a liquid, so entropy falls.

questions.prompt: What is the sign of ΔS for 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g), and why?
choices: Zero, because everything stays a gas
Positive, because the reaction releases energy
Positive, because the products are larger molecules
Negative, because 3 mol of gas become 2 mol of gas
questions.explanation: Fewer gas molecules means fewer ways to arrange matter and energy, so entropy decreases.
choiceExplanations: The number of gas moles changes, so ΔS isn't zero.
The sign of ΔH doesn't decide the sign of ΔS.
Fewer gas particles outweighs larger molecules.

choiceExplanations: −129.8 J/K ignores the coefficients.
This subtracts in the wrong order.
+583.7 J/K is only the reactants' total.

questions.prompt: Which has the greater standard molar entropy, Br₂(l) or Br₂(g)?
choices: It depends on the mass of the sample
They are equal, because they are the same substance
questions.explanation: Gas molecules move freely through a much larger volume, so the gas has more entropy.
choiceExplanations: The liquid's molecules are much less dispersed.
Standard molar entropy is per mole, so it doesn't depend on sample size.
The same substance in different states has different entropies.

questions.prompt: What does ΔG < 0 tell you about a process?
questions.explanation: A negative Gibbs free energy change means the process is favorable under those conditions.
choiceExplanations: At equilibrium, ΔG = 0.
ΔG < 0 can happen for endothermic or exothermic processes.
ΔG says nothing about the rate.

questions.prompt: A reaction has ΔH = −100. kJ and ΔS = −200. J/K. What is ΔG at 298 K?
choiceExplanations: This uses ΔS in J/K with ΔH in kJ.
This adds TΔS with the wrong sign.
This has the wrong overall sign.

questions.prompt: A reaction has ΔH > 0 and ΔS > 0. When is it thermodynamically favorable?
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS becomes negative once TΔS is larger than ΔH, which happens at high T.
choiceExplanations: That requires ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0.
That requires ΔH > 0 and ΔS < 0.
At low T the positive ΔH dominates, so ΔG > 0.

questions.prompt: A reaction has ΔH = +40.0 kJ and ΔS = +100. J/K. Above what temperature is it favorable?
questions.explanation: It becomes favorable when T > ΔH/ΔS = 40,000 J ÷ 100. J/K = 400. K.
choiceExplanations: 4000 K multiplies by 10 by mistake.
0.400 K mixes kJ with J/K.
2.50 K inverts the ratio.

questions.prompt: For a reaction with ΔG° < 0, what is true of its equilibrium constant K?
questions.explanation: ΔG° = −RT ln K, so a negative ΔG° requires ln K > 0, which means K > 1.
choiceExplanations: K = 1 goes with ΔG° = 0.
K < 1 goes with ΔG° > 0.
K is never zero.

questions.prompt: Diamond turning into graphite is thermodynamically favorable at room temperature, yet diamonds last essentially forever. Why?
choices: The reaction is actually unfavorable at room temperature
The reaction needs a catalyst to be favorable
The reaction has a very high activation energy, so it is extremely slow (kinetic control)
Diamond and graphite are at equilibrium
questions.explanation: Favorability (ΔG < 0) says nothing about rate. Breaking diamond's network of C–C bonds needs a huge activation energy.
choiceExplanations: The question states the reaction is favorable (ΔG < 0).
A catalyst changes the rate, not whether a reaction is favorable.
At room temperature graphite is more stable, so they aren't at equilibrium.

questions.prompt: An unfavorable reaction (ΔG° = +30 kJ) is coupled with a favorable one (ΔG° = −45 kJ) that shares an intermediate. What is ΔG° for the overall process?
choices: −15 kJ: the coupled process is favorable
questions.explanation: Free energies of coupled reactions add: +30 + (−45) = −15 kJ.
choiceExplanations: The overall ΔG° is the sum of both reactions' values.
−75 adds the sizes as if both were negative.
+75 subtracts the negative value.

choiceExplanations: 0.10 uses the wrong sign for ΔG°.
K = 1 would need ΔG° = 0.
2.3 is ln K, not K.

questions.prompt: In a galvanic cell, where does oxidation occur?
questions.explanation: Oxidation always happens at the anode, and electrons leave it through the wire.
choiceExplanations: Reduction happens at the cathode.
The salt bridge moves ions to keep the half-cells neutral; no redox happens there.
Electrons travel through the wire, but the reactions happen at the electrodes.

questions.prompt: Using E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, what is E°cell for Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s)?
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ is reduced (cathode) and Zn oxidized (anode): E° = 0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V.
choiceExplanations: +0.42 V adds the two potentials.
This subtracts in the wrong order.
−0.42 V adds them and flips the sign.

choiceExplanations: This divides by 1000 twice.
A positive E° gives a negative ΔG°.
−106 kJ uses n = 1.

questions.prompt: In the zinc–copper galvanic cell, [Cu²⁺] is increased while [Zn²⁺] stays the same. What happens to the cell potential?
choices: It stays the same, because E° doesn't change
questions.explanation: Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺]. More Cu²⁺ (a reactant) lowers Q, moving the cell further from equilibrium, so E rises above its previous value.
choiceExplanations: E° is fixed, but the actual potential E changes with concentrations.
Adding a reactant lowers Q.
E reaches zero only at equilibrium.

choiceExplanations: 0.318 g uses 4 electrons per Cu²⁺.
0.0100 is the moles of copper, not grams.
1.27 g uses 1 electron per Cu²⁺.

questions.prompt: How does an electrolytic cell differ from a galvanic cell?
choices: It uses an outside power source to drive a thermodynamically unfavorable reaction
It produces electrical energy from a favorable reaction
questions.explanation: Electrolysis forces a nonspontaneous redox reaction (ΔG > 0) using electrical energy.
choiceExplanations: Oxidation is at the anode in every electrochemical cell.
That describes a galvanic cell.
Electrolytic cells have an anode and a cathode.
